public_detail: Pinellas County Public Works-Urban Forestry and Landscape Services http://www.pinellascounty.org/publicworks/urban-forestry.htm Gallo v. Heller 512 So. 2d 215, 216 (Fla 3d DCA 1987) explains this common law rule as: The rule of common law and the majority rule in this county, which is followed in Florida, is that a possessor of land is not liable to persons outside of the land for a nuisance resulting from trees and natural vegetation growing on the land. The adjoining property owner to such a nuisance, however, is privileged to trim back, at the adjoining owner's own expense, any encroaching trees or branches and other vegetation that has grown onto his property. We are soliciting bids from vendors for tree trimming. All requests must be received by July 17, 2026, at 2:00 PM. Requests received after this deadline will not be included—no exceptions. To Request Tree Trimming: Submit a form at the front office or email tgordon@resourcepropertymgmt.com by the deadline. Include: Name, address, and phone number Tree type and location Whether the tree was trimmed last year Whether you need an estimate Important Information: You will be notified of the cost before trimming begins Previous requests are not carried forward—you must submit a new form Do not approach the tree-trimming crew directly; all requests go through the office Trimming will be completed in order and cannot be scheduled Individual invoices will be sent after completion; no advance payment required If you need to be present during trimming, please hire an outside vendor.
